# Talent.com Jobs and Salary Scraper - 78 Local Markets

Talent.com does not run one worldwide index. It runs a separate job site for each of 78 countries, and the site for a country carries that country's listings, currency and language. This actor works with every one of those sites: search by keyword and place, replay a search URL you already have, open individual job pages, or read the salary statistics Talent.com publishes for a job title and location.

Each job record is built from Talent.com's own structured job data, not from card text, so a record includes the full description when the site exposes it, the salary range as minimum/maximum/currency/period, city/region/country with latitude and longitude, remote status, O\*NET-SOC occupation code, the employer's apply URL, the publisher that supplied the listing and the date Talent.com first found it.

## Modes

| Mode | What it does |
|---|---|
| `search` | Run one or more keyword searches on a chosen country site, with optional location, distance, date, job-type, remote, Quick Apply and company filters. |
| `bySearchUrls` | Replay complete Talent.com search or category URLs and paginate them. Useful when a filter combination is easier to build in the browser. |
| `byJobUrls` | Open specific `/view?id=...` job pages (or pass bare numeric ids) and emit full job-detail records. |
| `salary` | Read the salary page for a title and place: percentiles, median, low/high, per-month/hour medians, related occupations and per-region medians. |

## What a job record contains

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `recordType` | `job` for search results, `jobDetail` for URL detail records, `salary` for salary statistics, `error` for an input or fetch failure. |
| `jobId`, `legacyJobId`, `jobUrl` | Numeric job id, Talent.com's older hexadecimal id, and the canonical job page URL on the same country site. |
| `title`, `normalizedTitle`, `company`, `companyLogoUrl` | Job title as published, Talent.com's normalized title, employer name and logo URL. |
| `location`, `city`, `region`, `countryCode`, `latitude`, `longitude` | Location string plus Talent.com's geocoded address and coordinates. |
| `salary`, `salaryMin`, `salaryMax`, `salaryCurrency`, `salaryPeriod`, `salaryIsPublic` | Salary text as shown on the site plus the structured band, ISO currency, period (`hour`, `month`, `year`, ...) and whether the pay is public. |
| `employmentType`, `employmentTypes` | Human-readable badge and a normalized list (`full-time`, `part-time`, `contract`, `temporary`, `internship`, ...). |
| `isRemote`, `workplaceType` | Remote flag and `remote`/`onsite`/`hybrid` when Talent.com identifies the workplace scope. |
| `postedAgo`, `dateFound`, `dateExpired`, `datePosted`, `validThrough` | Card age badge, Talent.com first-found/expiry timestamps, and the employer's posted/valid-through dates where the detail markup has them. |
| `description`, `descriptionSnippet` | Plain-text description and a short snippet. Snippets are always available from the search payload; the full text is added when the site exposes it or when `fetchFullDescriptions` is on. |
| `applyUrl`, `publisher`, `feedCode`, `isQuickApply`, `isPromoted` | Employer/ATS apply URL, the publisher that supplied the listing, its feed code, one-click Quick Apply flag and promoted-listing flag. |
| `onetCode`, `onetTitle`, `language` | O\*NET-SOC occupation code/title and the listing language. |
| `keyword`, `searchLocation`, `country`, `page` | The search that produced the record (omitted for URL/detail modes where it does not apply). |
| `scrapedAt` | When this record was collected, in ISO 8601 UTC. |

Salary records use `recordType=salary` and carry `jobTitle`, `location`, `country`, `countryCode`, `currency`, `totalSalaries`, `medianAnnual`, `lowAnnual`, `highAnnual`, `percentile10Annual`, `percentile25Annual`, `percentile75Annual`, `percentile90Annual`, `medianMonthly`, `medianHourly`, `relatedSalaries`, `regionSalaries`, `salaryPageUrl` and `scrapedAt`.

Every record is omit-empty: a field Talent.com does not provide for that posting is left out rather than written as `null`, `""` or an empty list. Salary values are never estimated by the actor.

## Input

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string | `search` | `search`, `bySearchUrls`, `byJobUrls` or `salary`. |
| `searchQueries` | array | – | One or more keywords. Each runs as its own search; results are deduplicated. |
| `keyword` | string | – | Single keyword (the legacy field). Combined with `searchQueries`. |
| `location` | string | – | City, state or region. Leave empty to search all locations. |
| `country` | string | `www` | Country site, one of 78. `www` is the United States. |
| `companyName` | string | – | Employer-name filter. Works on the US, Canada and UK sites only. |
| `radiusMiles` | integer | `25` | Radius in miles, 5-100; mapped to the site's 2/5/10/15/30/60-mile stops. |
| `datePosted` | string | – | `1`, `3`, `7`, `14`, `30` or `90` days. |
| `jobType` | string | – | `full-time`, `part-time`, `permanent`, `temporary` or `internship`. US/Canada/UK only. |
| `remoteOnly` | boolean | `false` | Remote jobs only, on the 10 country sites that support the filter. |
| `quickApplyOnly` | boolean | `false` | Quick Apply jobs only, on the same 10 sites. |
| `searchUrls` | array | – | Talent.com search/category URLs for `bySearchUrls`. |
| `jobUrls` | array | – | Talent.com job URLs or numeric ids for `byJobUrls`. |
| `fetchFullDescriptions` | boolean | `false` | Fetch each job page during a search to fill descriptions the search payload lacks. |
| `descriptionMaxLength` | integer | `0` | Truncate descriptions to N characters; 0 means full length. |
| `maxItems` | integer | `50` | Maximum job or salary records across the whole run. |
| `maxPages` | integer | `5` | Maximum result pages per search. |
| `proxyConfiguration` | object | `{"useApifyProxy": true}` | Optional; requests go direct first and use this proxy only after a block. |

### Example: search in the United States

```json
{
  "mode": "search",
  "searchQueries": ["software engineer", "data engineer"],
  "location": "New York, NY",
  "country": "www",
  "datePosted": "7",
  "remoteOnly": false,
  "maxItems": 100,
  "maxPages": 5
}
```

### Example: search another country site

```json
{
  "mode": "search",
  "keyword": "nurse",
  "location": "London",
  "country": "uk",
  "jobType": "full-time",
  "maxItems": 50
}
```

### Example: replay a saved search URL

```json
{
  "mode": "bySearchUrls",
  "searchUrls": [
    "https://www.talent.com/jobs?k=warehouse&l=Dallas%2C+TX&date=7",
    "https://uk.talent.com/jobs/k-nurse-l-london"
  ],
  "maxItems": 100
}
```

### Example: fetch specific jobs

```json
{
  "mode": "byJobUrls",
  "jobUrls": [
    "https://www.talent.com/view?id=626159695573821803",
    "645567462185641929"
  ]
}
```

### Example: salary statistics

```json
{
  "mode": "salary",
  "keyword": "software engineer",
  "location": "New York, NY",
  "country": "www"
}
```

The salary record for this example gives a median of 118,500 USD/year, a 99,375 low, a 185,000 high, p10/p25/p75/p90 values, monthly and hourly medians, ten related occupations and any per-region medians Talent.com publishes.

## Use cases

- **Job boards and aggregators** - refresh feeds from 78 country-specific Talent.com indexes with one schema.
- **Recruiting and sourcing** - monitor new postings for a role, company or city, and jump straight to the employer's apply URL.
- **Labour-market analysis** - group roles by O\*NET-SOC code, compare salary bands and remote mix between countries, map postings by coordinates.
- **Compensation research** - pair posting salary bands with the salary page's percentiles, medians and per-region values.
- **B2B lead generation** - identify employers hiring at volume in a city or occupation.
- **Career sites and alerts** - build a country-, keyword- or city-specific job feed without maintaining 78 parsers.

## Data source and independence

This is an independent actor. It reads Talent.com's public search, job and salary pages over HTTP; it is not affiliated with Talent.com. It does not log in, submit applications, solve CAPTCHAs, or use cookies. A proxy is optional and only used after a real block.

## FAQ and limits

**Why do some records have no salary?** Talent.com only publishes pay for a minority of postings, and the share differs by country and employer. When the site has no pay, `salary*` fields are omitted. The salary mode is the place to get market statistics for a title and place.

**Why fewer results than `maxItems`?** Talent.com has no total count and stops returning result pages after a few pages for a query (often 4-8 pages, about 20 jobs each). The actor pages until the site returns an empty page, retrying a transient empty page, then stops honestly. Narrow queries and multiple `searchQueries` give broader coverage.

**Why were some of my filters ignored?** Talent.com supports different filters per country. Job type and company only work on the US, Canada and UK sites; remote and Quick Apply work on 10 sites. Sending an unsupported filter makes Talent.com return zero jobs, so the actor skips it and reports the skip in the run status. The same applies to filters inside `searchUrls`.

**Why does the Canada site need special handling?** Plain HTTP requests to `ca.talent.com` receive a 403 from non-Canadian networks. The actor switches that site to a browser-impersonating HTTP client (no browser needed), so Canadian job search, job details and salary pages (CAD) work. This is verified live: 16 Toronto jobs parsed, a CAD salary median of 120,668 for software engineers, and the CA sitemap index returning 95 view/serp sitemaps.

**Why does the Russia site still behave differently?** `ru.talent.com` search and view pages redirect to a blocked page. The actor recovers jobs from the country's `view-ru-*` sitemap and reads each job through `/api/jobs/meta`, filtering by keyword/location client-side. Recovery is bounded (a few sitemap shards and up to 300 ids for large runs), so it can return fewer rows than a normal search. Russian salary pages remain unavailable. The other 76 country sites work normally.

**Are results sorted?** Talent.com no longer offers a sort control; its `sort` parameter is ignored. The legacy `sortBy` input is accepted but logged as ignored.

**Does it support incremental runs or notifications?** No. This actor is stateless and writes every matching record each run. Incremental change detection and Telegram/Slack webhooks are intentionally out of scope.

**Why did an `applyUrl` return a 404?** Talent.com supplies that link from the employer or its ATS. Some links go stale while the Talent.com listing stays live. The actor reports the URL exactly as the source provides it and never substitutes a Talent.com redirect or a fabricated link.

**Can it collect employer emails, phones or skills?** No. Talent.com's public job data does not include them, and the actor does not guess.

**Do I need an account or API key?** No. No login, cookie, API key or paid proxy is required.

**Why is a job URL from one country 404 on another?** Job ids are scoped to the country site. Keep the URL's own host; the actor does.
